configuration_map: The only geometric configuration is a single line segment of length 2p, bisected at M and cut unequally at N into segments a = p+q and b = p-q. N lies at distance q from M. All other objects (X, Y, f, rectangles, squares) are defined purely through algebraic area relationships (via 2.14, 6.1, 6.17). No triangles, circles, angles, or complex spatial figures are constructed. The proof operates entirely in the domain of commensurability theory and algebraic identities about lengths and areas.
skip_reason: The proof is purely algebraic and number-theoretic, dealing with commensurability relations, ratios of squares, and area identities. The only geometric construction is a trivial line bisection (Step 4) used to invoke the algebraic identity of Proposition 2.5. There are no angle decompositions, no interior/exterior point claims, no ray orderings, no circle position arguments -- none of the spatial configuration patterns that could produce contradictions. All reasoning is about whether ratios are or are not ratios of square numbers, and about commensurability of lengths and areas.
